title: Analytical mobility edge in nonreciprocal quasiperiodic lattices with next-nearest-neighbor hopping
authors: Wenmin Wang, Xiaosen Yang, Xianqi Tong
abstract: We investigate localization transitions and spectral topology in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian generalization of the Aubry-André model in which both the nearest-neighbor and the next-nearest-neighbor hopping amplitudes are nonreciprocal. By extending the Fermi-surface point-matching method to nonreciprocal hopping, we derive a closed-form expression for the energy-dependent mobility edge in which the two nonreciprocity parameters are absorbed into exponentially renormalized effective hopping amplitudes. The mobility edge forms a single parabola in the energy--potential plane: nearest-neighbor nonreciprocity rigidly shifts the localization boundary toward stronger potentials, whereas next-nearest-neighbor nonreciprocity reduces the curvature of the boundary and thereby broadens the energy window in which extended and localized states coexist. Exact diagonalization confirms the analytical boundary for purely nearest-neighbor, purely next-nearest-neighbor, and combined nonreciprocity, and recovers the known Hermitian mobility edge in the reciprocal limit. We further analyze the spectral topology under periodic boundary conditions and show that the spectral winding numbers evaluated at base energies near the two band edges directly bracket the mixed phase: the winding number at the lower band edge drops when the mobility edge enters the spectrum and the first localized states appear, while the winding number at the upper band edge drops when the last extended states localize, delineating the full potential-strength window over which extended and localized states coexist. These results provide a compact analytical framework that connects energy-dependent localization, spectral topology, and nonreciprocity in quasiperiodic lattices, and they are directly testable in photonic, atomic, and electrical-circuit platforms.
summary: This paper analytically determines the mobility edge in complex nonreciprocal quasiperiodic lattices featuring both nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor hopping. By extending established point-matching techniques, the authors derive a parabolic boundary that quantifies the transition between extended and localized electronic states. The findings are significant because they provide testable analytical tools connecting topological invariants (winding numbers) to transport properties in non-Hermitian systems.
main_problem: The study investigates localization transitions and spectral topology within nonreciprocal quasiperiodic lattices that include next-nearest-neighbor hopping.
main_result: The authors derive a closed-form, parabolic expression for the energy-dependent mobility edge, showing how nonreciprocity shifts and broadens the coexistence window of extended/localized states. Spectral winding numbers are used to precisely delineate this mixed phase.
method: The research extends the Fermi-surface point-matching method to handle nonreciprocal hopping, allowing for the derivation of effective hopping amplitudes and an analytical mobility edge formula.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional, non-Hermitian generalization of the Aubry-André model. It incorporates both nearest-neighbor (NN) and next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping terms, where the hoppings are made nonreciprocal via parameters $ eta$ and $\delta$.
key_observables: Mobility Edge ($E_c$), spectral winding numbers ($W(E_B)$), effective dispersion ($\epsilon(\kappa)$), and fractal dimension ($D_2$).
important_parameters: Nonreciprocity parameters ($ eta, \delta$), potential strength ($V$), hopping amplitudes ($t, J$), and the quasiperiodic frequency $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending the point-matching method to nonreciprocal hopping; quantitative comparisons suggest accuracy when NNN hopping is a perturbation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Hermitian limit comparison (analytical vs. numerical boundary), phase diagrams showing how NN and NNN nonreciprocity shift/widen the mobility edge parabola, and spectral topology plots using winding numbers to bracket the mixed phase region.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and the challenge of nonreciprocity. It then details the mathematical extension of the point-matching method to derive the analytical ME formula. Finally, it uses both exact diagonalization and topological invariants (winding numbers) to confirm the derived boundary and characterize the mixed phase.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly compact analytical framework connecting energy-dependent localization, spectral topology, and nonreciprocity in quasiperiodic systems, which is directly applicable to engineered photonic or electrical circuits.

The Biddle ME of Eq. (10) (black solid line) and the point-matching ME of Eq. (9) (red dashed line) are two analytical approximations to the same extended–localized boundary; both follow the numerical transition closely for J ≪t.

FIG. 2. Nonreciprocal phase diagrams (t = 1, J = 0.1, L = 610, PBC) together with the point-matching ME of Eq. (9) (red dashed lines). (a) NN nonreciprocity only, β = 0.25, δ = 0 (teff = e0.25 ≈1.28, Jeff = 0.1): the boundary shifts rigidly to larger V . (b) NNN nonreciprocity only, β = 0, δ = 0.25 (teff = 1, Jeff = 0.1 e0.25 ≈0.13): the curvature of the boundary decreases and the parabola widens. (c) Combined case, β = δ = 0.5: the shift and the widening superpose. In all three panels the analytical parabola, with no adjustable parameters, follows the extended–localized boundary.

FIG. 3. Skin-effect topology for NNN nonreciprocity (β = 0, δ = 0.25, t = 1, J = 0.1). (a) Spectral winding numbers W(EB) at two base energies near the band edges, EB = −2.0 (red) and EB = 2.8 (blue), as a function of V . The winding number at the lower band edge drops at V1 ≈1.6, marking the onset of the mixed phase where the ME enters the spectrum and the first localized states appear. The winding number at the upper band edge drops at V2 ≈2.6, marking the end of the mixed phase where the last extended states localize. FIG. 4. Solvable limits (L = 610, PBC). (a) J = 0, t = 1, β = 0.25: the localization transition is energy independent and occurs at Vc = 2t e|β| ≈2.57 (red dashed vertical line). (b) t = 0, J = 1, δ = 0.5: the transition is energy independent and occurs at Vc = 2J e|δ| ≈3.30 (red dashed vertical line). In both limits the ME degenerates into a vertical line, and no energy-dependent boundary exists. In (b) each eigenstate extends over a single sublattice, so the fractal dimension of extended states is slightly reduced, D2 ≈1 −ln 2/ ln L.

(9) with teff = e0.25 and Jeff = 0.1 e0.50. Although the imaginary gauge transformation maps the open chain to the Hermitian model, it is not single valued on the PBC ring: the bulk boundary is shifted to larger V relative to the Hermitian Biddle line [whose E = 0 crossing lies at V ≈1.98, versus V ≈2.65 for the parabola] and is well described by the effective-hopping parabola.
